subject: BrightEdge: minute-scale surge capacity — pricing options and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Torres <atorres@brightedge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@brightedge.com
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Short notice: minute-scale capacity bump for holiday test

Hi Mina —

We have a planned stress test for our recommendation service on Wednesday (launch rehearsal) and the infra team expects minute-level surges for a 6–8 hour window. Can Redwood provide a short-term capacity bump (peak concurrency) to avoid throttling?

Key asks:
- Capacity target: +2.5k concurrent inference QPS for the 6–8h window (expected ~18M tokens/day during the window)
- Need: instantaneous lift by Wednesday 08:00 PST, revert after the window
- Pricing: we need a clear overage / burst rate and any discount if we commit to a follow-up pilot or 3-month commit

We don’t have a PO in place for this one-off. If there’s an escrow/true‑up route or a prepaid slab, share options. Attachments: none.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Torres
Product Ops, BrightEdge
atorres@brightedge.com

On behalf of BrightEdge launch team
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@brightedge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Short notice: minute-scale capacity bump for holiday test

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the details. We can support a minute-scale surge but there are a few viable billing flows depending on how BrightEdge prefers to settle: prepaid slab, one-time overrun true‑up, or a provisional short‑term uplift with an early‑payment credit if you convert to a 3‑month commit after the test. I’ve outlined two options you can pick from quickly.

Option A — Ephemeral slab (fastest, no PO required):
- 48-hour ephemeral slab reserved for the window, capacity +2.5k QPS (reverts automatically)
- Price: $1,800 per qps-hour (covers reserved capacity; billed as a one-time line item) — estimated charge for 8 hours: $14,400
- Add-on: 10% credit if you convert to a 3‑month paygo commit within 14 days (applied retroactively)

Option B — Overrun true-up (post-facto billing):
- No reservation. We allow temporary throttle lift; usage counts as overrun and is billed at $35 / million tokens for the surge window
- Estimated cost for expected volume (~18M tokens): ~$630 (note: token-based billing is lower but lacks capacity guarantee)

Operational notes:
- We’ll require an approval from finance for Option A since it involves a one-time invoice without a PO; Laura can advise on the quickest path.
- We can apply soft throttles + proactive alerting so you won’t drop requests unexpectedly.
- Attached a quick pricing matrix and a draft SOW for Option A to this thread.

If you’re comfortable, say which option and I’ll push for approvals and scheduling. If you prefer, we can do a hybrid: ephemeral slab for the rehearsal window + token true-up for any overspill.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Alex Torres <atorres@brightedge.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 13:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Short notice: minute-scale capacity bump for holiday test

Looping in a quick alternative pricing structure that helped with a similar pilot last quarter. Two quick points: we can soften the ephemeral slab rate if the customer agrees to a short promotional commitment (no legal amend needed, just an email confirmation).

Counter-proposal (Option A-1) — Promo slab discount:
- Same 48-hour ephemeral slab and QPS target
- Promotional price: $1,200 per qps-hour (33% off) if BrightEdge confirms a 90-day paygo track at equivalent commit within 7 days after the rehearsal
- Fallback: if conversion doesn’t happen within 7 days, charge reverts to $1,800 per qps-hour but we’ll only bill the delta up to the original date (i.e., we won’t invoice retroactively beyond the rehearsal window)

Procurement note (Laura): if we need a PO, can finance accept a one-off invoice with net-30 while we spin a short SOW? If a PO is required before provisioning, we’ll need a very accelerated sign path — Mina, I can approve the promotional slab verbally for now but will need written confirmation from BrightEdge after.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@brightedge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Short notice: minute-scale capacity bump for holiday test

Alex — Per Ben, we can offer a promotional ephemeral slab to keep your rehearsal safe and make conversion cheaper if you follow up with a 90-day commit. Summary and next steps below. I’ve attached the SOW and the pricing matrix for procurement.

Final offer (Option A-1, promotional):
- 48-hour ephemeral slab / +2.5k QPS (auto-revert)
- Promotional rate: $1,200 per qps-hour — estimated charge for an 8-hour window: $9,600
- Condition: BrightEdge confirms conversion to a 90-day paygo commit at similar throughput within 7 calendar days after the rehearsal (email confirmation to our deals inbox is OK)
- If conversion does not happen: invoice is adjusted to $1,800 per qps-hour; we only bill the delta for the rehearsal window

Procurement path:
- If you can provide a PO before provisioning, we’ll accept net-30 and issue a one-time invoice on completion.
- If a PO is not possible, we can provision on a good‑faith credit hold; billing will follow the invoice path above and we’ll require a billing contact and an internal contact for escalation.

I attached: burst-pricing-matrix.xlsx (breakdown by qps-hour and token true‑up) and BrightEdge_ephemeral-slab_SOW_v1.pdf (one-page SOW + acceptance criteria). Attachments: 
- burst-pricing-matrix.xlsx (pricing sheet)
- BrightEdge_ephemeral-slab_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW)

Please reply with: (1) accept Option A-1, (2) accept Option B (token true-up), or (3) request hybrid. If accepted, we’ll provision and send the invoice draft.

Thanks — Mina
